newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA DISMANTLES OVERSIZED STATE-RUN OIL HOLDING.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA DISMANTLES OVERSIZED STATE-RUN OIL HOLDING.

text.p: Romania's government has dismantled the oversized National Oil Company and replaced it with a new firm grouping an oil extraction company, two refineries and a retailer firm, a top official said on Tuesday.
"The new Societatea Nationala a Petrolului "Petrom SA" (SNP) will not have a monopolistic position on the market," Industry Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu told reporters.
The creation of the SNP is part of moves by the new centrist government to streamline the oil sector, in line with suggestions made by international lenders.
Romania's refining industry, with a capacity of 34 million tonnes, inherited from the former communist regime, is the largest in central and eastern Europe.
To become effective, the government decision has to be published in the Official Gazette.

The SNP's backbone is the Petrom RA oil authority which extracts all Romania's crude oil and around 35 percent of the country's natural gas. The refineries of Petrobrazi SA and Arpechim SA and the Peco SA petroleum products retailer are also part of the new SNP.
"The project has been designed with help from the Paribas bank and was endorsed by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development," Tariceanu said.

The SNP replaces the former National Oil Company holding, created in 1995 by the former leftist cabinet, which grouped the country's 10 refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies and oil exploration company.
An initial plan backed by the World Bank suggested the inclusion of only one refinery within the new company.
"The CRP was unviable and produced huge losses. The new company will work solely on commercial basis," Tariceanu said.

The SNP would conclude contracts to supply crude oil to the other refineries in the country which would work "independently in order to ensure demand is met on the local market", a government statement said.
Romania produces annually some six million tonnes of crude oil and imports around the same quantity each year.

Petrobrazi, in the Ploiesti oilfield, and the Pitesti-based Arpechim can process together up to seven million tonnes of crude annually. Each refinery has a reserve capacity of 3.5 milion tonnes per year, currently mouthballed.
Peco owns some 43 percent of Romania's retailer network.
Arpechim's pipelines can get only one million tonnes of locally-produced crude, data show. The remaining 2.5 million has to be imported through the oil terminal in the Black Sea port of Constanta.
Tariceanu said building new pipelines to connect Arpechim to Romania's oilfields would be among SNP's priorities.
